Name: Milan Malpensa T1 — arrive & depart
Notes: Land 19:00 D1. Depart ~23:00 D15. Eat landside here on arrival night. Be at the rental return lot by 20:00 on D15 — confirm the return terminal matches your flight terminal.

Name: HSM Hotel San Martino — Garbagnate Monastero
SearchQuery: HSM Hotel San Martino Garbagnate Monastero
Notes: Nights 5-8 Oct. 24h reception, free parking, no restaurant. ~500 m off the SS36 — ask for a room away from the road.

Name: Birra & Brace — late option near the hotel
Notes: D1 hedge. Roadside grill/pizzeria 2 min from the hotel, the kind of place that stays open late. Have reception (+39 031 851700) ring ahead — Monday is the standard closing day in Brianza. Better plan: eat at Malpensa.

Name: Dac a Tra' — Michelin star, 10 min from the hotel
SearchQuery: Dac a Tra Castello di Brianza
Notes: The closest starred restaurant to your base. Contemporary, produce-driven. +39 039 5312410.

Name: Villa del Balbianello — Lenno
Notes: D2. Gardens ~EUR13-14, + 45-min interior tour ~EUR24-25. CLOSED Mon AND Wed — this is why the west shore goes on Tuesday. Book the interior tour ahead.

Name: Villa Carlotta — Tremezzo
Notes: D2. Open daily, 10:00-19:00 to 18 Oct. ~EUR15-17.50. Real art inside (Canova, Hayez) — the one villa that survives a wet day.

Name: Bellagio — ferry pier & old town
Notes: D2 afternoon. Arrive as a foot passenger from Cadenabbia. Villa Melzi gardens EUR10, open to 19:00. Golden hour 17:45-18:55.

Name: Sunset boat — Bellagio / Varenna
Notes: D2. Private hour ~EUR150-200, or shared from ~EUR40pp. October light on this lake is the best of the year. Book ahead — October fleets are reduced.

Name: Lido di Lenno — car park for Balbianello
Notes: D2. SET THE SATNAV HERE, not to the villa. The taxi-boat (~EUR6) and the 20-25 min woodland path both start here. Paid blue lines.

Name: Free parking — uphill streets, Lenno / Mezzegra
Notes: D2 free option. White-line residential streets uphill off the SS340. 10-15 min walk down. Read the signs — anything yellow is residents-only.

Name: Cadenabbia ferry pier — park & walk on
Notes: D2. Leave the car here and walk on as a foot passenger. DON'T put it on the car ferry — you don't need it in Bellagio and it costs several times a foot ticket.

Name: Como Duomo + Museo della Seta — wet-day swap
Notes: D2 RAIN PLAN. The Duomo is free and one of the great Gothic/Renaissance hybrids in Italy. The silk museum is far better than it sounds — Como was the silk capital of Europe. Also Tempio Voltiano, Basilica di Sant'Abbondio. Skip the Brunate funicular: you'd pay to sit in a cloud.

Name: Il Cavatappi / Vecchia Varenna
Notes: D3 dinner. Il Cavatappi is tiny, in a stone alley — the romantic one. Vecchia Varenna is on the water in a former black-marble works. Varenna after dark is the prettiest village on the lake.

Name: Sentiero del Viandante — Varenna start (Olivedo)
Notes: D3. ~3h, ~530 m ascent to Bellano. Up Via della Croce from Olivedo, via Vezio and Regolo. POLISHED LIMESTONE — genuinely slippery wet; don't do it in a downpour.

Name: Orrido di Bellano — gorge walkway
Notes: D3, end of the walk. EUR8 adult. Lit walkway bolted into a gorge. Better with more water in it, but CAN CLOSE on high water — check before driving over.

Name: Villa Monastero — Varenna
Notes: D3. Garden + house museum EUR15, garden only EUR13. Last entry 17:30. CLOSED TUESDAYS — hence Varenna on Wednesday. Furnished period rooms = indoor option.

Name: Lecco Wednesday market — Piazza Garibaldi
Notes: D3 alternative, 07:30-14:00, 50+ stalls. Runs 4 Mar - 25 Nov 2026. Wednesday 7 October falls perfectly in your stay.

Name: Varenna-Esino-Perledo station — THE smart park
Notes: D3. Free or near-free, 10 min walk down into Varenna — AND it's exactly where your train back from Bellano drops you. No backtracking, no second fee, no uphill walk after a 3-hour hike.

Name: Perledo — free roadside parking above Varenna
Notes: D3 free fallback. White lines on the road up to Perledo. 10-15 min down, 20-25 min back up.

Name: Olivedo / Varenna pier lots — paid fallback
Notes: D3 paid fallback. ~EUR2/h or EUR12-15/day in high season, usually cheaper and less strictly enforced in October. NEVER drive into Varenna's centre — the lanes are stairs.

Name: Accademia Carrara, Bergamo — best wet day on the Como leg
Notes: D3 RAIN PLAN. Botticelli, Bellini, Raphael, Titian. SWAP WEDNESDAY AND THURSDAY and do Bergamo today — it costs nothing because Thursday's Bergamo stop was optional anyway. Plus arcaded Citta Alta, Santa Maria Maggiore, Cappella Colleoni.

Name: Lecco museums — Villa Manzoni & Palazzo delle Paure
Notes: D3 local rain option. EUR6 each. Villa Manzoni is the family home of the man who wrote Italy's national novel about THIS shore. Lecco's Wednesday market (Piazza Garibaldi, 07:30-14:00) is thin in heavy rain.

Name: Bergamo Citta Alta — Piazza Vecchia
Notes: D4 lunch stop, directly on the A4. Funicular up ~EUR3 return, every 5-10 min. Eat casoncelli alla bergamasca. NEVER drive up — hard ZTL plus Lombardy emissions rules.

Name: Piazzale Cappello degli Alpini — Monte Barro
Notes: D4. Free weekday parking right at the trailhead. The EUR5 shuttle from the Fornace lot only runs on busy weekends.

Name: Eremo di Monte Barro — free parking + view
Notes: D4. 14th-c. hermitage with a restaurant and terrace, drivable. The panorama with zero walking if you're short on time.

Name: Fiera di Bergamo — 300 FREE spaces
Notes: D4. 300 free spaces, served by bus line 1 into the centre. The cheap answer for Bergamo. CONFIRMED from the operator.

Name: Ex Bonini — free P+R, Via San Bernardino 149
Notes: D4. ~150 spaces, bus line 6. Second free option for Bergamo.

Name: Bergamo funicular base — Viale Vittorio Emanuele II
Notes: D4. Where the funicular to Citta Alta starts. ~EUR1.50 single / EUR3 return, every 5-10 min, runs 06:00 to past midnight.

Name: Paid garages — Ex Gasometro / Baschenis / Stadio
Notes: D4 paid, closer in. Ex Gasometro (312 spaces), Via Baschenis (71), underground Stadio Atalanta at Piazzale Goisis (348, MAX HEIGHT 2.20 m). All open 24/7.

Name: The Oswald Grand Hotel — Selva di Val Gardena
SearchQuery: The Oswald Grand Hotel Selva di Val Gardena
Notes: Nights 8-12 Oct. PIN IS APPROXIMATE — confirm the exact address, and ask about the Selva restricted-traffic zone and plate registration.

Name: Nives — Selva village square
SearchQuery: Ristorante Nives Selva di Val Gardena
Notes: CONFIRMED OPEN YEAR-ROUND, which in this valley in October is not a small thing. South Tyrolean + Mediterranean, homemade pasta. +39 0471 773329.

Name: Seceda — the ridge
Notes: D5. THE most weather-dependent day of the trip — in cloud you pay for fog. Ridge walk 8.9 km, +575 m, 3-3.5h. Move it to any clear day in the block.

Name: Col Raiser gondola — Santa Cristina (CHEAPER ROUTE)
SearchQuery: Col Raiser Santa Cristina Val Gardena
Notes: D5 preferred start. Runs to 1 Nov, materially cheaper than the EUR74 Ortisei cable car, far quieter. From the top walk up via Pieralongia (~+400 m, 1h15-1h30) — this is the bit the closed Fermeda chairlift used to do.

Name: Ortisei–Furnes–Seceda cable car (CLASSIC ROUTE)
Notes: D5 alternative. ~EUR74 return, first up 08:30. Fastest way to the famous view. Park at the station — Ortisei centre is one of the longest pedestrian zones in the Dolomites.

Name: Rifugio Firenze / Regensburgerhutte
Notes: D5 lunch. CLOSES 12 OCTOBER — one of your last chances. Service 11:30-15:00. Reachable ~25 min on path 4 from the top of Col Raiser.

Name: Cristauta / Praplan — fully-on-foot Seceda start
Notes: D5 hardcore option. Trail 4 up to the ridge — but with FERMEDA CLOSED it's a +900-1,000 m climb with no shortcut. Real, but a big first day in the mountains.

Name: Otzi — South Tyrol Museum of Archaeology, Bolzano
SearchQuery: Museo Archeologico Alto Adige Bolzano Otzi
Notes: THE best wet-weather destination of the whole trip, ~50 min down the valley from Selva. The 5,300-year-old iceman found in a glacier up the road. Use it for whichever Val Gardena day is a write-off. Bolzano also has the arcaded Portici and the Duomo.

Name: Vallunga — flat, low, forested, fine in drizzle
Notes: Val Gardena drizzle option, straight from Selva. Flat gravel track up a glacier-carved valley under the Puez walls, 2.5h return, larches everywhere. Pay-and-display at Parcheggio Vallunga. Also the D8 slow-morning fallback.

Name: Abbazia di Novacella — monastery + winery
Notes: Augustinian monastery with a rotunda library, baroque church AND its own winery doing tastings. Historic, indoors, wine — arguably a better rainy morning than the hike is a sunny one.

Name: Cantina Tramin — Termeno
Notes: One of Italy's best co-ops in a striking modern building. Tastings in the wine shop WITHOUT booking, Sat 09:00-17:00, closed Sunday. An hour south — hard to combine with Val di Funes.

Name: Adolf Munkel Weg — Zannes/Zans trailhead
Notes: D6 morning. 9.2 km circuit, +378 m, 3-3.5h, easy-moderate, along the base of the Odle north wall. ZANNES CAR PARK MAY NEED AN ONLINE BOOKING IN 2026 — check before driving up.

Name: Chiesa di Santa Maddalena — Val di Funes
Notes: D6. The most photographed building in South Tyrol. NON-RESIDENT CARS ARE BARRED from the panorama viewpoint May-Nov — park in the village and walk 20-30 min.

Name: Torggelen — Villandro / Villanders
Notes: D6 afternoon, 15 min from Zannes. Certified farms: Oberpartegger, Winklerhof, Pschnickerhof — linked by walking trails. PHONE AHEAD: season nominally starts early Oct but many farms open mid-month. Indoors = rain-proof.

Name: Geisler Alm / Rifugio delle Odle
SearchQuery: Geisler Alm Rifugio delle Odle Villnoss
Notes: D6. You flagged this as a 'no go' — I'd push back gently. It's directly ON the Adolf Munkel Weg, so you pass its door regardless. The busy/commercial complaint is a high-summer problem. THE REAL RISK IS THAT IT'S SHUT — October season unverified.

Name: Zannes / Zans car park — Val di Funes
Notes: D6. PRE-BOOKABLE ONLINE IN 2026 — check whether Sat 10 Oct needs a reservation before you drive up.

Name: Forcella Sassolungo 'coffin' gondola — Passo Sella
SearchQuery: Forcella Sassolungo cable car Passo Sella
Notes: D7, 09:30. CLOSES 11 OCTOBER — you cross this pass on the 12th, one day too late. Two-person standing cabins that never stop; 5 min up to Rifugio Toni Demetz at 2,681 m. Date is single-sourced — VERIFY EARLY. Wind can hold it even in clear weather.

Name: Alpe di Siusi / Compatsch
Notes: D7 afternoon. Up to 14.4 km, +483 m, 4.5h, easy. Europe's largest high meadow. Best in low afternoon light. Open huts: Sassopiatto (to 18 Oct), Alpe di Tires (to 19 Oct), Schgaguler (to 1 Nov).

Name: Mont Seuc gondola — Ortisei (use this one on D7)
SearchQuery: Ortisei Alpe di Siusi cable car
Notes: D7. Runs to 2 Nov, and it's the side you arrive from after Passo Sella. DON'T DRIVE UP to Compatsch — road closed to non-residents 09:00-17:00 and parking needs an online reservation.

Name: Passo Sella — free parking
Notes: D7 and D8. Free parking at the pass, at the foot of the coffin gondola. 20 min from Selva.

Name: Terme Merano — the cold/wet Sunday answer
Notes: D7 RAIN PLAN, ~1h15 from Selva. Large thermal complex, indoor AND outdoor pools, big sauna world. Being outside in hot water in cold rain is not a consolation prize. Merano has covered arcades and the Kurhaus too.

Name: B&B Hotel Passo Tre Croci — Cortina
SearchQuery: B&B Hotel Passo Tre Croci Cortina
Notes: Nights 12-16 Oct, at 1,805 m. The Lago di Sorapis trailhead is at the door. Hard frost most nights. Ask them about trail 215 ice conditions.

Name: El Brite de Larieto — on the Tre Croci road
Notes: D8 dinner, effectively on your doorstep. Agriturismo with its own dairy. Open until late October, CLOSED WEDNESDAYS. Book: +39 368 7008083.

Name: Lago di Carezza / Karersee
Notes: D8, ~09:30. Emerald lake reflecting the Latemar. Paid car park on the SS241 with an underpass to the shore; boardwalk loop 20-30 min. GO EARLY — you need still water, and the coaches arrive late morning. No swimming, no going to the water's edge.

Name: Canazei — Val di Fassa
Notes: D8, ~11:00. Main town of the Ladin Val di Fassa, at the hub of the four great passes. Coffee and lunch stop. Sass Pordoi cable car almost certainly closed by now.

Name: Segra Sacun market — Ortisei, 12 Oct only
Notes: D8 FALLBACK, 08:00-16:00. The biggest traditional market of the year — food stalls, crafts, and a tradition of men giving women a decorated pear. CLASHES with the 08:00 Great Dolomites Road start; you can't have both. Take it if you want a slow morning or it rains.

Name: Lago di Carezza car park — SS241
Notes: D8. Paid pay-and-display on the SS241, with an underpass to the lake shore.

Name: Passo Sella — 2,244 m
Notes: Crossed twice: D7 for the coffin gondola, D8 on the Great Dolomites Road. Sassolungo fills the windscreen the whole way up. 20 min from Selva. Free parking.

Name: Passo Pordoi — 2,239 m
Notes: D8, ~12:45. Sass Pordoi cable car above it almost certainly closed by mid-October — bonus, not a plan.

Name: Passo Falzarego — 2,105 m
Notes: D8 and D11. Free parking, and the base of the Lagazuoi cable car — the only lift still running in Cortina. Kept open through winter, so October is never in doubt.

Name: Passo Gardena — 2,121 m (short route + sunset)
Notes: The short-route alternative for D8. Also the best zero-effort sunset of the Val Gardena leg — Sassolungo framed by golden larches, 15 min from Selva.

Name: Passo Campolongo / Arabba — short route
Notes: On the short pass route (Gardena - Corvara - Campolongo - Arabba - Falzarego, 85 km, 2h45), the fallback if you skip Carezza and Canazei.

Name: Valley fallback — Val Pusteria via Dobbiaco
Notes: D8 SNOW FALLBACK. Ponte Gardena - A22 - Val Pusteria - Dobbiaco - SS51. 145 km, ~2h20 — actually FASTER on the clock than the passes, just far less beautiful. Check venetostrade.it and the Bolzano traffic portal that morning.

Name: Brunico / Bruneck — Messner Mountain Museum Ripa
Notes: D8 RAIN PLAN, on the valley fallback route. Handsome market town; the castle holds MMM Ripa, on the mountain peoples of the world. CHECK OCTOBER HOURS.

Name: Lago di Braies / Pragser Wildsee
Notes: D9, arrive ~08:00. Sunrise 07:26 — leave the hotel at 07:00. Still water, empty boathouse, coaches still an hour out. Shore loop 3.5 km flat, ~1h. NO RESERVATION NEEDED IN OCTOBER (that system runs 1 Jul-15 Sep). Survives mist well.

Name: Tre Cime di Lavaredo — Rifugio Auronzo
SearchQuery: Rifugio Auronzo Tre Cime di Lavaredo
Notes: D9. BOOK THE SLOT at pass.auronzo.info — EUR40/car, plate required, 12h validity, autumn access ~08:00-18:00. Loop 8.8-10 km, +425 m, 3-4h anticlockwise. ~700 spaces at the rifugio.

Name: Cadini di Misurina viewpoint
Notes: D9, add-on. 3.9 km, +144 m, 1-1.5h on trail 117 from Rifugio Auronzo. THE FINAL SPUR IS A NARROW, EXPOSED PATH ON A ROCK NOSE — dry conditions only, skip it if there's frost or fresh snow.

Name: Rifugio Locatelli — CLOSED, no food or shelter
Notes: D9. CLOSED for the season. It sits at the far side of the Tre Cime loop, so there is no food, water or shelter for the middle two-thirds. Wind at Forcella Lavaredo is brutal in October — carry everything.

Name: Lago di Misurina — 10-minute stop
Notes: D9. Directly on the Tre Cime road and you pass it twice — take whichever light is better. The Grand Hotel Misurina reflected with the Sorapis group behind. Col de Varda chairlift closed 20 Sep.

Name: Tre Cime toll gate — Misurina
Notes: D9. EUR40 per car, PRE-BOOKED ONLINE ONLY at pass.auronzo.info. Plate required, ticket valid 12h. 5 km up to Rifugio Auronzo from here.

Name: Lago di Braies — lakehead parking
Notes: D9. Paid pay-and-display at the lakehead. No reservation needed in October.

Name: San Candido / Innichen — church + Acquafun pool
Notes: D9 RAIN PLAN — bail north instead of east. Beautiful Romanesque collegiate church, and Acquafun indoor pool/wellness centre. CHECK HOURS. Save the EUR40 and book Tre Cime for another day — this is exactly why you don't book it early.

Name: Dobbiaco / Toblach — Mahler & cultural centre
Notes: D9 rain option, on the way back from Braies. Gustav Mahler composed here; the Grand Hotel is now a cultural centre.

Name: SanBrite — Michelin star, 'agricucina'
Notes: Everything from the family farm, own cheese dairy. Tasting EUR90-120. Sister to El Brite, 10 min from Passo Tre Croci. CALL +39 0436 863882 to confirm October opening.

Name: Baita Fraina — above Cortina
Notes: D10 dinner (El Brite is closed Wednesdays). Mountain-lodge regional cooking in small panelled rooms, Michelin Guide listed.

Name: Lago Federa / Croda da Lago
SearchQuery: Lago Federa Rifugio Croda da Lago
Notes: D10. THE most famous larch location in the Dolomites, 2,046 m. Rifugio Croda da Lago / Palmieri is the most reliable hut lunch of the Cortina leg — call +39 0436 862085. Overcast light is GOOD for larches.

Name: Ponte de Ru Curto — Lago Federa trailhead
Notes: D10 start. Free trailhead parking. 8.4 km / +469 m / 3h out-and-back, or the 13.1 km / +700 m / 5h circuit.

Name: Lago di Sorapis — FLEX day, from the hotel door
SearchQuery: Lago di Sorapis Passo Tre Croci
Notes: FLEX. Trailhead is at Passo Tre Croci. 11.5 km out-and-back, ~500 m, ~4h. TRAIL 215 HAS CABLED EXPOSED LEDGES, METAL LADDERS AND POLISHED ROCK, all north/east-facing and shaded — ICED LADDERS ARE A REAL OCTOBER RISK. Rif. Vandelli closed 20 Sep: no water, shelter or toilet. Mildest driest day only, mid-morning start, CARRY MICROSPIKES, turn back if there's ice. Ask the hotel the night before.

Name: Cortina museums — Zardini fossils & Rimoldi art
Notes: D10 RAIN PLAN. Museo Paleontologico Rinaldo Zardini (these mountains are a fossilised coral reef — a good thing to learn while looking at them) and the Mario Rimoldi modern art collection, both in the Ciasa de ra Regoles. Small municipal museums — CHECK OCTOBER HOURS.

Name: Rifugio Ospitale — SS51 north of Cortina
Notes: 11th-century hospice turned restaurant, road-accessible, tends to have a longer season than the mountain huts. A good long-lunch answer on a wet day.

Name: Lagazuoi cable car — Passo Falzarego
Notes: D11. THE ONLY LIFT STILL RUNNING in Cortina — to 18 Oct. Free parking at the pass. First up 09:00, every 15 min, LAST DOWN 17:00. Terrace lunch at 2,752 m — call +39 0436 867303.

Name: Cinque Torri — WWI open-air museum
Notes: D11. Restored trenches and tunnels among the five towers. CHAIRLIFT CLOSES 11 OCT and all three huts (Scoiattoli, Nuvolau, Cinque Torri) are shut — walk up from Col Gallina and carry food.

Name: Col Gallina — free parking, Cinque Torri trailhead
Notes: D11. Free parking on the SR48 opposite Ristorante da Strobel. Circuit 9.6 km, +600 m, ~3h45 via Lago di Limedes to Rif. Averau, Nuvolau and Cinque Torri. Nuvolau's final ridge is narrow with a cable.

Name: Monte Mondeval from Passo Giau — full-day option
Notes: D11 alternative. 12.8 km, ~5h, moderate, open and panoramic, larch-rich. A full-day substitute for the Lagazuoi/Cinque Torri pair.

Name: Val Travenanzes descent from Lagazuoi
Notes: D11 alternative. Cable car up, walk down a wild hanging valley to Ponte Outo on the SR48 — 4-5h, mostly descent, some cabled steps near the forcella. NEEDS A CAR SHUTTLE.

Name: Passo Giau — 2,236 m
Notes: D11 return leg. Come home over Giau on the SP638 instead of retracing Falzarego — same time, makes the day a loop. Bare amphitheatre under Ra Gusela and Nuvolau; larches rivalling Lago Federa. Rifugio Fedare at the top is OPEN YEAR-ROUND.

Name: Forte Tre Sassi — WWI museum, Passo Valparola
Notes: D11 RAIN PLAN. A restored Austro-Hungarian fort covering exactly the WWI front you'd have been walking at Cinque Torri and Lagazuoi — with a roof. Seasonal: CHECK OCTOBER HOURS.

Name: Venice — stay in Dorsoduro or Cannaregio
Notes: Night 16 Oct. NOT YET BOOKED. Dorsoduro for romance (Zattere at sunset), Cannaregio for easy logistics. Stay on the island, not Mestre.

Name: All'Arco — San Polo 436
Notes: D13, 11:00. Standing-room counter, no written menu, everything made that morning. EUR1.50-4 each. NO RESERVATIONS, CLOSED SUNDAY, and the shutters come down ~14:00 when the trays are empty.

Name: Osteria alla Vedova — Cannaregio
Notes: D12 evening. The legendary deep-fried polpetta. EUR2-5 a cicchetto. Closed Thursday (fine for you). Carry cash.

Name: Vino Vero — Fondamenta Misericordia
Notes: D12 evening. Natural wine bar, crostini with stracciatella, anchovy, lardo. Open daily 12:00-24:00.

Name: Al Timon — Fondamenta dei Ormesini
Notes: D12 evening. Everyone sits on the canal edge and on the moored boat. Daily 11:00-01:00.

Name: Antiche Carampane — the big dinner
Notes: D12, 20:30. The one with the sign saying no pizza, no lasagne, no tourist menu. Outstanding fried fish. ~EUR70-90pp. BOOK WEEKS AHEAD. Closed Sun-Mon, so Friday works.

Name: Tronchetto parking — Venice
Notes: D12, arrive ~14:00. EUR29 per 24h, covered, 3,483 spaces. MAX HEIGHT 2.10 m — check your car isn't a tall SUV. Easiest arrival: you never leave the causeway. People Mover to Piazzale Roma ~EUR1.50.

Name: Rialto market
Notes: D13, 09:00. Saturday morning is the good one — fish, produce, noise. All'Arco is a minute away.

Name: Gallerie dell'Accademia — Venice
Notes: D12 rain plan, minutes from a Dorsoduro hotel. Venice is genuinely rain-proof; the October risk is ACQUA ALTA, not rain. Check the city tide forecast the night before and buy rubber overshoes.

Name: Peggy Guggenheim Collection
Notes: D12 rain plan. Modern art on the Grand Canal, a few minutes from the Accademia.

Name: Scuola Grande di San Rocco — Tintoretto
SearchQuery: Scuola Grande di San Rocco Venezia
Notes: D12 rain plan. Tintoretto's entire cycle, in the room he painted it for. One of the great interiors in Europe and never crowded.

Name: Lake Garda — south-west shore
Notes: Nights 17-19 Oct. NOT YET BOOKED. Salo / Desenzano / Sirmione / Padenghe — all ~2h to MXP. Shortlist: Bellerive (Salo), Acquaviva (Desenzano), Villa Arcadio (Salo hills).

Name: Sirmione ZTL — Parcheggio Grifo / Monte Baldo
Notes: D13-14. The Sirmione peninsula is a 24/7 CAMERA ZTL, year-round. Hotel guests MUST email their plate 24-48h ahead and keep the confirmation. Non-guests park here, outside the gate.

Name: Valeggio sul Mincio — 'nodo d'amore' tortellini
Notes: D14 lunch, 15 min from Peschiera. Home of tortellini di Valeggio, the love-knot, with its own legend about a nymph and a knight. About as on-theme as a honeymoon lunch gets.

Name: Guerrieri Rizzardi — Bardolino
Notes: D14, 15:00. Aristocratic estate, tastings DAILY 10:00-18:30 — one of the very few open on a Sunday. From ~EUR15 for 90 min. Book: visite@guerrieri-rizzardi.it.

Name: Cantina Zeni wine museum — Bardolino
Notes: D14. Free museum and enoteca, no booking needed — the one drop-in option on the lake.

Name: Grotte di Catullo — Sirmione
Notes: D14, 09:30. Vast Roman villa ruin in an olive grove at the tip of the peninsula, water on three sides. Go early, before the coaches. OPEN RUIN — the one thing on D14 that rain ruins.

Name: Castello Scaligero — Sirmione
Notes: D14. Water-moated Scaliger castle guarding the entrance to the old town. Sirmione at night, once the day-trippers have gone, is the good version.

Name: Aquaria Thermal SPA — Sirmione
Notes: D14 RAIN PLAN, and the best one on the trip. Sulphurous thermal spring, indoor and outdoor pools, five minutes from the castle. Everything else on D14 already has a roof: the winery, the olive oil museum, the Valeggio lunch.

Name: Verona — Arena, Castelvecchio, Duomo
Notes: D14 rain option, 30 min from Sirmione. Mind the ZTL: Mon-Fri 10:00-13:30 and 16:00-18:00, Sat-Sun 10:00-13:30. Park at Cittadella.

Name: Museo dell'Olio d'Oliva — Cisano
SearchQuery: Museo dell'Olio di Oliva Cisano Bardolino
Notes: D14. Free museum and shop, open daily. Mid-October is the start of the Garda DOP olive harvest.

Name: Zenato — Peschiera del Garda
Notes: D15, 10:00. Lugana AND Valpolicella/Amarone under one roof — the best single tasting on the lake. Classic tour EUR40 (4 wines + food, 90 min). MON-SAT ONLY, booking essential.

Name: Franciacorta — Ca' del Bosco / Bellavista, Erbusco
Notes: D15, ~13:00. Italy's best metodo classico, ~40 min along the A4 towards MXP. Turns dead driving time into the last good thing you do. WHOEVER DRIVES DOESN'T TASTE.
